# Enforced Engineering Rules

This is the agent-readable trigger index for rules enforced by Maestro and for
requirements a generated customer must preserve. It separates mechanical
blockers, local authoring checks, conditional gates, and advisory review so
workers run the right proof before a change becomes expensive.

Executable authorities are the copies present in the current repository, such as
`package.json`, `eslint.config.mjs`, `.qlty/qlty.toml`,
`dependency-cruiser.config.cjs`, `tooling/quality/`, `tooling/acceptance/`, and
`.woodpecker/`. `docs/rule-coverage.md` is an enforcement map, not an executable
authority. Re-read configuration and implementation when either document
disagrees with code. Never weaken a red gate to match documentation.

Before Convex work, also read
`packages/convex/convex/_generated/ai/guidelines.md`; its current API guidance
overrides remembered Convex patterns.

## Enforcement Postures

| Posture              | Meaning                                                                                               |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Mechanical blocker   | Compiler, test, scanner, AST check, or deterministic CI failure; repair before delivery               |
| Local authoring gate | Changed-file or focused command required when its trigger applies                                     |
| Conditional gate     | Required only after the named artifact or trust boundary changes                                      |
| Advisory review      | Qlty/AI/human finding; repair new owned-code findings, while deterministic CI remains merge authority |

## Scope And Customer Projection

This document is shipped to generated customers, but not every factory control
is shipped with it:

- Product architecture, generator, Cucumber, type-safety, lifecycle, headless,
  security, and dependency requirements apply when the corresponding surface
  exists in the current checkout.
- Factory hook, Qlty triage, Woodpecker, release, and protected dependency-proxy
  details describe this source repository. Current customer ownership omits
  `.woodpecker/`, `.qlty/`, and `tooling/ci/`; those controls do not become
  customer enforcement until a reviewed customer-owned projection installs them.
- Run commands only when they exist in the current checkout. The current
  checkout's `AGENTS.md`, package scripts, and CI policy win over factory paths
  named here.

For this factory, Woodpecker is the sole blocking CI authority and the required
GitHub context is `ci/woodpecker/pr/verify`. Buildkite is retired. Fabro is not
an execution plane. Qlty is required while authoring new code but remains
advisory for merge scheduling under repository policy. A generated customer must
install and activate its own CI/quality projection before claiming either the
factory status or equivalent supply-chain coverage; current customer ownership
does not include `.woodpecker/`, `.qlty/`, or `tooling/ci/`.

## Required Generator Loop

For every table, capability, workflow, agent, or user-facing Feature:

1. Run `pnpm maestro -- preflight --mode fake` from a clean customer target.
2. Run `pnpm maestro -- recipes list`.
3. Run `pnpm template:systems -- --query <responsibility-or-table>` and record
   `reuse`, `extend`, or a reviewed system introduction.
4. Preview the direct generator named by the relevant playbook.
5. Preview the reviewed scaffold:

       node maestro-template.mjs scaffold \
         --generator <generator-id> \
         --args '<exact-json-object>'

6. Inspect collisions, privacy posture, generated bytes, provenance, codegen,
   and focused gates.
7. Execute the returned `confirmation.argv` unchanged. It binds the write to
   exact `preflight_sha256:` and `scaffold_sha256:` fingerprints.
8. Run every emitted focused gate and the behavior tests for the slice.
9. Commit generated provenance/receipts with the implementation.

Preflight requires a clean target. Complete and commit one generator transaction
before previewing the next; do not batch several generator writes behind one
preflight fingerprint. Run a user-facing Feature generator before specializing
same-name capability or UI files, and invoke each generator once.

Never append `--write` manually to a direct generator. Never hand-copy a
generated slice or hand-edit a generated authority to hide drift.

## Cucumber Product Contracts

- `features/**/*.feature` is the sole customer-journey authority.
- Each Feature has exactly one `@wip` or `@required` tag.
- Each Scenario has exactly one `@ui`, `@cli`, or `@cross_surface` tag.
- A required Feature has at least one cross-surface Scenario.
- `pnpm maestro -- contracts check` compiles tags and dry-runs **all** Features.
  `@wip` does not hide undefined or ambiguous steps.
- Create a Feature with its initial bindings at the beginning of the slice that
  implements it.
- Real UI and CLI use one disposable backend. Fakes exist only at external
  provider boundaries.
- In the reference records contract, the runner holds one ephemeral API key, the
  CLI sends it directly, and Vite's server-side proxy attaches it for UI
  requests; browser code never receives the key. A customer may replace that
  fixture with its real auth boundary, but must keep both surfaces on the same
  backend and keep credentials out of browser code.
- The checker validates tags and Gherkin shape only. Cucumber execution and
  human review own whether a `@cross_surface` Scenario actually drives both
  surfaces with declarative, useful steps; the tag alone is not proof.
- Steps never seed product rows, bypass operations, or use an in-memory product
  substitute.
- Promote to `@required` only after `contracts test <journey>` passes. Run
  `contracts test --required` on the frozen delivery head.
- Cucumber retries and parallelism are both zero. Fix flakes; do not mask them.
- Do not add a journey manifest, evidence store, progress registry, or custom
  acceptance controller beside Cucumber.

Triggered commands:

    pnpm acceptance:features
    pnpm maestro -- contracts check
    pnpm maestro -- contracts test <journey>

## Qlty Thresholds

Qlty smells are block mode for new files and new rule/path pairs:

| Rule                | Threshold |
| ------------------- | --------: |
| Identical code      |  12 lines |
| Similar code        |  15 lines |
| Function complexity |        10 |
| File complexity     |        50 |
| Return statements   |         5 |
| Boolean logic       |         4 |
| Function parameters |         5 |
| Nested control flow |         4 |

Gitleaks and OSV also run in block mode. Qlty monitor scope is mixed: broad
copied-source entries cover `releases/**` and `examples/**/seed/source/**`, and
additional entries name existing rule/path pairs. New findings outside those
scopes block the local command; findings inside them remain monitored. Do not
widen monitor scope to land product code.

Keep work below thresholds while authoring: use an input object before a sixth
parameter, guard clauses or small pure helpers before a fifth nested branch, and
real shared helpers for structural duplication. Do not create an abstraction
merely to silence a short domain-specific resemblance.

    pnpm check:qlty -- --staged
    pnpm check:qlty -- --diff

The local wrapper gives each spawned Qlty subprocess 30 seconds. `--diff` runs
`check` and `smells` separately, so the wrapper invocation can exceed 30
seconds. Provider/runtime failure remains advisory to merge scheduling;
deterministic Woodpecker evidence is authoritative.

## TypeScript, ESLint, Effect, And Formatting

- TypeScript is strict with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
  `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and `noImplicitOverride`.
- Type coverage must be at least 99.7%.
- Explicit `any`, non-null assertions, `@ts-ignore`, and `@ts-nocheck` are
  errors. Described `@ts-expect-error` directives are accepted by the current
  lint rule and exist in deliberate compile-time negative fixtures; do not use
  them to suppress implementation defects. Avoid `as unknown as`; it evades
  useful typing.
- Do not add `eslint-disable`. An unavoidable inherited boundary requires a
  constraint comment and reviewed backlog note.
- Effect diagnostics reject floating Effects, missing error/context types,
  missing service dependencies, missing return/yield, and leaked requirements.
- Prettier owns formatting.

The actual pre-commit hook auto-formats staged files, runs shift-left ESLint,
and runs staged Qlty. Pre-push runs repository typecheck, lint, dependency and
structural gates. Effect diagnostics and type coverage run in `pnpm verify`;
they are not pre-commit commands.

Changed TypeScript authoring proof is:

    pnpm prettier --check <changed-files>
    ESLINT_SHIFT_LEFT=1 pnpm eslint <changed-files>
    pnpm typecheck
    pnpm check:effect-diagnostics
    pnpm check:types-coverage

`ESLINT_SHIFT_LEFT=1` makes complexity 10, depth 4, and parameter count 5
blocking for changed files. Pass only the task-owned changed TypeScript paths;
repository-wide `pnpm lint` is not a substitute and can make unrelated legacy
debt look like a task regression.

## Confect, Effect, And Workflow Rules

- Public, internal, and HTTP functions use Confect specs/impls with typed args,
  returns, and expected errors.
- Every external operation declares public typed errors and includes
  `ValidationFailed` for input-envelope validation.
- Public manifest metadata declares operation kind, allowed principals, minimum
  role/scope, exposure, idempotency posture, bounds, and secret-bearing output.
  Projections consume that manifest rather than a second registry.
- Specs use type-only imports for plain Convex functions; runtime values belong
  in impl files.
- Expected failures use typed result/error channels. Do not throw tagged errors
  under `packages/convex/confect` or bare `Error` across callable boundaries.
- Workspace writes declare a minimum role. Time is injected/owned; do not use
  ambient `Date.now()` in Confect implementation code.
- Domain files are flat: sibling runtime imports are forbidden; top-level
  `import type` is allowed.
- Workflows call capabilities. They never call provider adapters, repos, raw
  database operations, environment, or fetch directly.
- Author every workflow through reviewed `template:add-workflow`.
- Application code never imports `@convex-dev/workflow`, creates a
  `WorkflowManager`, hand-rolls Workflow primitives, or calls raw
  `ctx.scheduler.runAfter`/`runAt`.
- Policy-dependent runs pin exact policy version and hash at kickoff; replay
  never reads “latest”.
- Outbox delivery uses a generated workflow/component/cron boundary, not raw
  scheduling.

Generated workflow paths are:

- `packages/convex/confect/workflowContracts/<name>.{spec,impl}.ts`
- `packages/convex/confect/workflows/<name>/v1.graph.ts`
- `packages/convex/confect/workflowRunners/<name>/v1.{ts,spec.ts,impl.ts}`
- generated `packages/convex/convex/workflowRunners/<name>/v1.ts`
- `packages/convex/test/<name>.workflow.test.ts`
- generated semantics JSON and Markdown

Triggered commands:

    pnpm confect:codegen
    pnpm confect:manifest
    pnpm check:confect-contracts
    pnpm check:confect-manifest
    pnpm check:workflow:fast
    pnpm check:workflow-semantics
    pnpm check:workflow-graph-boundary

## Architecture, Frontend, Provider, Environment, And Logging

- `apps/web` cannot import Convex/Confect internals. Feature modules cannot
  import route modules. `packages/workflow-ui` cannot import the hosted app.
- Production code cannot import `experiments/` or `private-packages/`.
- Routes remain declarative composition; product state, hooks, browser globals,
  time/randomness, and derivation live below the route.
- Frontend Effect execution occurs only in
  `apps/web/src/adapters/effectBoundary.ts`.
- Provider SDK imports stay inside approved adapters. Prefer native `fetch` and
  add no provider SDK for a small HTTP boundary.
- Runtime environment values are decoded only at approved central boundaries.
  Adapters receive typed config and never read `process.env`.
- Add each provider secret/config name to `docs/template/env-manifest.json`, its
  Markdown projection, and central decoded config in the same task.
- Runtime code under `apps/` and `packages/` cannot call `console.*`; use typed,
  redacted observability or explicit CLI output seams.
- UI work covers loading, empty, ready/read, ready/edit, mutation success, and
  mutation failure when applicable, plus keyboard/focus/accessibility basics.

Triggered commands:

    pnpm check:layer-boundaries
    pnpm check:route-tree
    pnpm check:frontend-effect-boundary
    pnpm check:env-boundary
    pnpm check:provider-boundary
    pnpm check:logging-boundary
    pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck

## Systems, Tables, Lifecycle, And Generated Ownership

- Every hand-authored table has exactly one canonical system owner.
- Use reviewed `template:add-table` for every durable table.
- Table arguments include canonical system, `extend` disposition, tenant scope,
  sensitivity, PII class, export/delete modes, retention, append-only posture,
  business-entity posture, and description.
- A new system requires a reviewed decision under
  `docs/template/system-decisions/`, canonical entrypoint, catalog entry, and
  topology update before generators may use its ID.
- Table changes include schema-migration decisions and complete lifecycle
  metadata in the same change.
- Lifecycle metadata is not execution. Every personal-data resource supplies a
  handler through the existing lifecycle authority, and tests prove suppression,
  export, expiry, subject deletion, workspace deletion, and cross-store cleanup
  for its rows, files, vectors, and analytics facts. A dry-run-only plan is not
  a shipped deletion path.
- Regenerate `packages/convex/confect/ops/dataResources.generated.ts`; never
  edit it.
- Append-only tables are insert-only. Raw `db.delete`, `db.patch`, and
  `db.replace` are forbidden across canonical Convex roots except the exact
  component-local allowances already checked by the repository. The reviewed
  lifecycle authority is the sole documented redaction/deletion exception and
  must emit an immutable audit tombstone.
- Route trees, Confect/Convex output, manifests, data-resource runtime, workflow
  semantics/docs, release payloads, and provenance remain generator-owned.

Triggered commands:

    pnpm data-resources:generate
    pnpm check:schema-migration-notes
    pnpm check:system-catalog
    pnpm check:system-topology
    pnpm check:data-resources
    pnpm check:append-only-tables
    pnpm check:promotion-boundary
    pnpm check:confect-contracts

## Headless API, CLI, And MCP

The generated Confect manifest is the only operation authority. Do not add
`productOperations.ts` or any second operation manifest.

- Reviewed feature, capability, and workflow generators emit starter
  CRUD/`run`/lifecycle methods. Those methods are scaffolding, not implicit
  product API. Remove or internalize every method not named by the owning plan
  before manifest generation; exact-set parity tests reject both missing and
  extra exposed operation IDs.
- Extend `operationRefs` in `packages/convex/confect/http.ts`,
  `staticCliOperationRefs` in `apps/cli/src/index.ts`, and
  `generatedMcpOperationRefs` in `tooling/workflow/src/index.ts`.
- Dispatch through `executeHeadlessOperation`; no canned-success registry path.
- Preserve exact generated-ref parity across exposed surfaces.
- Internal operation IDs are not web/API/CLI/MCP exposed.
- The agent catalog is an explicit manifest exposure class. Exact-set parity
  applies to that product-agent set; inherited web-only/platform operations may
  remain in the manifest but must not leak into CLI or generic MCP discovery.
- Non-idempotent external mutations/actions enforce a nonblank idempotency key.
  Scope it by principal, tenant/subject binding, and operation; persist a
  canonical input hash; reject same-key/different-input; and define replay and
  retention semantics.
- Authenticate and reauthorize the current principal/resource before consulting
  an idempotency record. Revocation must prevent replay from revealing an old
  result.
- Extend the smallest generated auth metadata needed for principal and scope; do
  not invent another router.
- Business inputs never accept tenant IDs as authority. Session/headless
  adapters derive and check actor, tenant, subject, and scope. A transport slug
  may be a checked routing assertion but is not forwarded as business identity.
- Unknown operation IDs and input properties fail closed.
- Secret-bearing operations are never invokable through generic MCP. Their CLI
  adapter requires an explicit output path, creates it with owner-only
  permissions, and keeps the secret out of stdout; their UI adapter uses an
  authorized no-store response. Do not build a second secret-delivery service.

Triggered commands:

    pnpm check:headless-surface-contract
    pnpm --dir apps/cli test
    pnpm --dir tooling/workflow test
    pnpm check:confect-manifest

## Security, Privacy, Files, And Analytics

The mechanically checked baseline is narrower than the product contract:

- `check:secret-canaries` runs Gitleaks with redaction.
- `check:env-boundary` and `check:logging-boundary` scan their named source
  roots.
- `check:access-audit-events` currently pins member and invitation lifecycle
  audit paths.
- `check:auth-demo-bypass` is a shape pin, not a complete authorization proof.

The remaining requirements below are conditional product requirements. When a
slice introduces the named boundary, its plan must name focused behavioral and
negative tests plus review against `docs/template/security.md`,
`docs/template/security-threat-model.md`, `docs/template/data-lifecycle.md`, and
`docs/template/data-map.md`. The five commands listed after this section do not,
by themselves, prove every clause.

- No runtime auth-bypass marker. Tenant-membership reads include a tenant guard;
  HTTP dispatch fails closed; production source maps remain disabled.
- Tenant, actor, subject, side, API-key scope, and resource ownership are
  server-derived.
- Raw keys, provider/webhook secrets, and credentials are never committed,
  logged, attached to Cucumber output, put in client storage, or stored
  unhashed. A claim invitation may carry its one-time token only in the URL
  fragment: the landing code removes it synchronously with
  `history.replaceState` before loading third-party resources and submits it in
  an authorized request body. It never appears in the path, query, referrer,
  telemetry, analytics, or attachment.
- A deliberately authorized one-time TLS response may reveal a new key/token
  with `Cache-Control: no-store`; it must never enter persistence, browser
  history, telemetry, analytics, or attachments.
- Uploads use a narrow authenticated capability. Before linking a Convex
  `_storage` ID, query the system table and validate uploader/resource
  ownership, size/type, and one-time intent. Raw downloads reauthorize every
  request, use a verified MIME allowlist, force attachment disposition for
  untrusted content, and send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.
- Convex owns PII, raw source material/provider payloads, evidence indexes,
  vectors, File Storage, and transactional state.
- Analytical stores receive normalized non-authoritative facts only: no direct
  PII, raw text, provider payload, or unrestricted property bag. External
  subject IDs are HMAC-pseudonymized at the narrowest reporting scope that
  supports the accepted journey; broader cross-campaign linkage requires a new
  reviewed purpose.
- Model-provider calls minimize/redact personal data, use an allowlisted
  no-training/no-retention provider posture, and persist a non-content receipt
  naming model/provider, policy and prompt hashes, data classes, and redaction
  counts. If that posture cannot be proved, the live model path stays disabled.
- Money facts include currency. Missing data lowers coverage; it never becomes
  zero.
- Browser tracking strips query/fragment from path/referrer, caps strings and
  event-type cardinality, rejects unknown/PII-like properties, and never
  fingerprints.
- Attribution cookies are first-party and use `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`,
  `Path=/`, no `Domain`, and bounded `Max-Age`.
- Identity-bearing PII reads require an explicit PII scope and an audit event.
  Ordinary operators may add legal suppression, but only the privacy/admin
  lifecycle authority may clear it with a new lawful basis and reason.
- Exports are bounded, audited, and authorized. Sensitive CLI exports require an
  explicit owner-only local output file and never print row data to stdout; UI
  exports use an in-memory download. Do not create permanent public URLs.
- Citation URLs strip fragments and non-allowlisted query parameters. Persist a
  stable public locator/provider object ID, never a signed provider URL.
- Gitleaks runs with redaction; fixtures use obvious short fake values.

Triggered commands:

    pnpm check:auth-demo-bypass
    pnpm check:secret-canaries
    pnpm check:access-audit-events
    pnpm check:env-boundary
    pnpm check:logging-boundary

## Dependency And CI Supply Chain

Factory CI details in this section are not customer enforcement until a
customer-owned CI/quality projection exists.

- Runtime is Node `22.12.0`; package manager is pnpm `10.12.1`.
- CI uses frozen offline installs with lifecycle scripts ignored.
- `.pnpmfile.cjs` is forbidden.
- Lockfile artifacts are HTTPS-only from `registry.npmjs.org`, size-bounded,
  integrity-checked, redirect-free, allowlisted, and inspected.
- Build scripts are restricted by `onlyBuiltDependencies`; Knip rejects unused
  dependencies. Gitleaks and OSV block the local Qlty command when the checkout
  owns `.qlty/qlty.toml`.
- A new dependency requires demonstrated need, lockfile/allowlist updates,
  license and vulnerability review, frozen-install proof, Knip, and Qlty. Prefer
  native APIs or installed packages.
- Never invoke Buildkite or launch Fabro. Never manufacture or reinterpret CI
  status.

The proof is deliberately split:

- `check:deps` pins core package metadata and lockfile presence; it is not a
  full dependency audit.
- `check:sbom-license` pins the checked-in dependency/license inventory; human
  review owns license acceptability.
- Qlty/OSV supplies vulnerability findings where that projection is installed.
- Factory setup and candidate-sandbox paths own the frozen offline install and
  protected artifact allowlist. A generated customer must provide equivalent
  evidence through its own CI before claiming that coverage.

Triggered commands after a dependency change:

    pnpm check:deps
    pnpm check:knip
    pnpm check:sbom-license
    pnpm check:qlty -- --diff

## Trigger Matrix

| Changed area          | Minimum focused gates in addition to tests                                            |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Feature or steps      | `acceptance:features`, `contracts check`, named `contracts test`                      |
| TypeScript            | Prettier, shift-left ESLint, focused typecheck, Qlty                                  |
| Confect spec/impl     | codegen, manifest, contracts, Effect diagnostics                                      |
| Exposed operation     | manifest, headless surface, CLI and MCP/workflow tests                                |
| Table/index/lifecycle | data-resource generation, migration notes, catalog/topology, lifecycle, append-only   |
| Workflow              | workflow fast check, semantics, graph boundary, generated workflow test               |
| Provider/config       | env, provider, logging, secret, adapter tests                                         |
| Route/UI              | route tree, layer/Effect boundaries, web typecheck, state/accessibility tests         |
| Dependency            | metadata pins, Knip, inventory + human license review, OSV, allowlist, frozen install |
| Frozen customer batch | clean-head required Cucumber execution plus one `pnpm verify`                         |

## Frozen-Head Verification

In a generated customer repository that contains accepted Features, run focused
tests per task. Freeze a clean delivery head, record its SHA, then run the full
required proof once:

    git diff --check
    git status --short
    git rev-parse HEAD
    pnpm maestro -- contracts test --required
    pnpm verify

`pnpm verify` does not run required Cucumber Scenarios. The explicit contracts
command above first validates required Feature shape and then executes
`cucumber-js --tags @required`.

The template/factory source repository has no root `features/` directory and
must not run that customer command. Its separate projection evidence is the
generator suite plus `apps/cli` create-root integration in
`tooling/ci/verify-chassis.sh`; those tests materialize disposable customer
targets and prove the emitted Feature/contract commands. `check:generators` is a
static descriptor check included in factory `pnpm verify`; it does not require
live Convex codegen.

Use any host-specific semaphore or remote wrapper required by the enclosing
`AGENTS.md`, not by this portable template document.

## Worker Stop Conditions

Stop and repair the plan or authority when:

- a required path or operation exists only in a plan, not the generated target;
- a generator preview reports an unexpected collision or owner;
- work needs caller-supplied tenant/subject authority;
- a workflow needs provider/database/environment work in replayed code;
- a table lacks lifecycle or migration metadata;
- a lifecycle resource still reports dry-run-only or has no behavioral cascade
  test;
- an undefined Cucumber step is hidden by a tag;
- a new framework, registry, provider abstraction, queue, database, object
  store, or dependency is proposed for one implementation; or
- a red gate would require suppression or gate-file edits instead of repair.
